reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

votes.question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendments — An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes (H R 5334)
votes.plain_language: The House voted to accept the Senate's rewrite of H.R. 5334, which imposes Russia-related sanctions and tariffs, extends an Iran sanctions law, and also expands a teacher tax deduction to early-childhood educators. A Yea accepts that Senate version. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 93)
votes.plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress authorizes it, except for forces needed to defend against an imminent attack if the President follows the War Powers Resolution's time limits. A Yea agrees. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Whistleblower Protection Act (H R 4646)
votes.plain_language: This bill extends whistleblower protections to employees of Housing and Urban Development contractors and grantees, including on contracts signed before 2013. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Table — Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors (H RES 1486)
votes.plain_language: The resolution would impeach President Trump over Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection practices that it says violate the Constitution. This vote was a motion to table, which kills the resolution. A Yea tables it; a Nay would have left it pending.

lobbying.bill_title: Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors.

votes.plain_language: This resolution condemns the actions of those seeking to defraud the U.S. government. A Yea agrees to the resolution; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Stopping Fraudulent Payments Act (H R 8464)
votes.bill_title: Stopping Fraudulent Payments Act
votes.plain_language: This bill establishes requirements to prevent fraudulent or improper payments from federal programs. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Stopping Fraudulent Payments Act (H R 8464)
votes.bill_title: Stopping Fraudulent Payments Act
votes.plain_language: H.R. 8464 (Stopping Fraudulent Payments Act) establishes requirements to prevent fraudulent or improper payments from federal programs. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Passage — Fraud Prevention and Accountability Act (H R 8312)
votes.bill_title: Fraud Prevention and Accountability Act
votes.plain_language: This bill assigns improper-payment prevention and spending-transparency functions to the Treasury's Bureau of the Fiscal Service, creates an Office of the Inspector General for Fraud, Accountability, and Recovery within Treasury, and requires Treasury data-sharing agreements with other agencies and allowable private entities to prevent fraud and improper payments. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Retirement Fairness for Charities and Educational Institutions Act (H R 1013)
votes.bill_title: Retirement Fairness for Charities and Educational Institutions Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: Official question: On Passage. H.R. 1013: Retirement Fairness for Charities and Educational Institutions Act of 2025. Result: Passed.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Fostering the Use of Technology to Uphold Regulatory Effectiveness in Supervision Act (H R 8278)
votes.bill_title: Fostering the Use of Technology to Uphold Regulatory Effectiveness in Supervision Act
votes.plain_language: This bill orders federal banking regulators to study whether their technology can supervise firms in real time and whether buying new systems is slowed by procurement rules. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Main Street Act (H R 6955)
votes.bill_title: Main Street Capital Access Act
votes.plain_language: This bill lessens and otherwise modifies banking regulations, including those regarding institution formation, supervision by federal financial regulators, and bank merger requirements. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Main Street Act (H R 6955)
votes.bill_title: Main Street Capital Access Act
votes.plain_language: H.R. 6955 (Main Street Capital Access Act) lessens and otherwise modifies banking regulations, including those regarding institution formation, supervision by federal financial regulators, and bank merger requirements. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Passage — Protecting Privacy in Purchases Act (H R 1181)
votes.bill_title: Protecting Privacy in Purchases Act
votes.plain_language: This bill prohibits payment card networks from using merchant codes that distinguish firearms retailers from general-merchandise retailers or sporting-goods retailers. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — Protecting Privacy in Purchases Act (H R 1181)
votes.bill_title: Protecting Privacy in Purchases Act
votes.plain_language: H.R. 1181 (Protecting Privacy in Purchases Act) prohibits payment card networks from using merchant codes that distinguish firearms retailers from general-merchandise retailers or sporting-goods retailers. A motion to recommit is the minority's last formal chance to send a bill back to committee before the passage vote. A Yea supports sending it back; a Nay keeps it on the floor for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — TRIA Program Reauthorization Act (H R 7128)
votes.bill_title: TRIA Program Reauthorization Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill reauthorizes the Terrorism Risk Insurance Program through 2034. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Financial Exploitation Prevention Act (H R 2478)
votes.bill_title: Financial Exploitation Prevention Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill establishes procedures for delaying the redemption of certain securities if an investment company or agent believes that an older individual or an individual with certain impairments has been financially exploited. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — American Enrichment Deployment Act (H R 9612)
votes.bill_title: American Enrichment Deployment Act
votes.plain_language: Official question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended. H.R. 9612: American Enrichment Deployment Act. Result: Passed.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Nuclear REFUEL (Recycling Efficient Fuels Utilizing Expedited Licensing) Act (H R 3978)
votes.bill_title: Nuclear REFUEL (Recycling Efficient Fuels Utilizing Expedited Licensing) Act
votes.plain_language: Official question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended. H.R. 3978: Nuclear REFUEL (Recycling Efficient Fuels Utilizing Expedited Licensing) Act. Result: Passed.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Ratepayer Protection Act (H R 9340)
votes.bill_title: Ratepayer Protection Act
votes.plain_language: This bill tells state utility regulators to consider making very large power users, such as data centers using 100 megawatts or more, pay the full extra cost of grid upgrades built to serve them. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Protecting Domestic Mining Act (H R 1501)
votes.bill_title: Protecting Domestic Mining Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill puts mining infrastructure projects into the FAST Act's faster environmental-review process and blocks a proposed rule that would have limited which mining projects qualify. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

votes.question: On Passage — Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to “California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Ocean-Going Vessels At-Berth; Notice of Decision” (H J RES 210)
votes.bill_title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Environmental Protection Agency relating to "California State Nonroad Engine Pollution Control Standards; Ocean-Going Vessels At-Berth; Notice of Decision".
votes.plain_language: This resolution would cancel the Environmental Protection Agency decision that let California tighten emissions rules for ocean-going ships while they are docked. A Yea votes to cancel that decision. A Nay votes to leave it in place.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Diesel Emissions Reduction Act (H R 2140)
votes.bill_title: Diesel Emissions Reduction Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill reauthorizes Environmental Protection Agency grants through fiscal year 2029 to replace old diesel engines or add pollution controls. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Local Communities & Bird Habitat Stewardship Act (H R 3276)
votes.bill_title: Local Communities & Bird Habitat Stewardship Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill writes into law the Urban Bird Treaty program, including grants to help cities conserve birds. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendments — An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes (H R 5334)
votes.bill_title: Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: The House voted to accept the Senate's rewrite of H.R. 5334, which imposes Russia-related sanctions and tariffs, extends an Iran sanctions law, and also expands a teacher tax deduction to early-childhood educators. A Yea accepts that Senate version. A Nay rejects it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 93)
votes.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.
votes.plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress authorizes it, except for forces needed to defend against an imminent attack if the President follows the War Powers Resolution's time limits. A Yea agrees. A Nay rejects it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 89)
votes.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran.
votes.plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress has declared war or authorized that force, while still allowing defense against an imminent attack. A Yea agrees to that direction. A Nay rejects it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities in Lebanon (H CON RES 108)
votes.bill_title: Directing the President pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities in Lebanon.
votes.plain_language: This concurrent resolution directs the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities in Lebanon within seven days of the resolution's adoption. A Yea agrees to the concurrent resolution; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — KIDS Act (H R 7757)
votes.bill_title: KIDS Act
votes.plain_language: This bill requires specified online platforms to establish safeguards for minors. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Small Business Technological Advancement Act (H R 915)
votes.bill_title: Small Business Technological Advancement Act
votes.plain_language: This bill authorizes the Small Business Administration to finance, under its 7(a) loan program, business software or cloud computing services, including tools that use artificial intelligence. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Small Business Lending Fraud Prevention Act (H R 7401)
votes.bill_title: Small Business Lending Fraud Prevention Act
votes.plain_language: This bill requires Small Business Administration employees who take part in originating, reviewing, or approving agency loans to certify in writing that they have no conflict of interest with the loan and to disclose any conflict that arises later. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — National Fraud Enforcement Division Act (H R 9576)
votes.bill_title: National Fraud Enforcement Division Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill gives a permanent statutory home to the Justice Department office that investigates fraud against taxpayer-funded programs. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — GUARD Act (H R 2978)
votes.bill_title: GUARD Act
votes.plain_language: This bill lets law-enforcement grants be used on financial fraud, elder fraud, and "pig butchering" crypto scams, and it asks the Treasury's financial-crimes office for reports. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Prison Staff Safety Enhancement Act (S 307)
votes.bill_title: Prison Staff Safety Enhancement Act
votes.plain_language: This bill requires the Justice Department to set standards for preventing and punishing sexual harassment and assault of federal prison staff by incarcerated people, and to carry out an inspector general's recommendations. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Protect Economic and Academic Freedom Act (H R 4795)
votes.bill_title: Protect Economic and Academic Freedom Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill would bar colleges that take federal student aid from commercial boycotts of Israel, and it would require colleges that take certain foreign-language funds to treat programs in Israel like programs in other countries. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

votes.question: On Passage — No Aid for Ghost Students Act (H R 7892)
votes.bill_title: No Aid for Ghost Students Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill requires the Department of Education to establish an identity fraud detection system for the Free Application for Federal Student Aid. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Whistleblower Protection Act (H R 4646)
votes.bill_title: Whistleblower Protection Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill extends whistleblower protections to employees of Housing and Urban Development contractors and grantees, including on contracts signed before 2013. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Concur in Senate Adt to House Adt to Senate Adt — Housing for the 21st Century Act (H R 6644)
votes.bill_title: 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act
votes.plain_language: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act establishes and modifies various federal housing programs. This vote, under suspension of the rules, was on accepting the Senate's latest changes to the bill after the chambers traded versions, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea accepts the Senate's version; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to require that the Supreme Court of the United States be composed of nine justices (H J RES 1)
votes.bill_title: Proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States to require that the Supreme Court of the United States be composed of nine justices.
votes.plain_language: This resolution proposes a constitutional amendment fixing the Supreme Court at nine justices. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports that amendment; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Local Access to Courts Act (S 32)
votes.bill_title: LACA
votes.plain_language: This bill adds College Station, Texas, and El Centro, California, as places where specified federal courts must sit. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Emergency Conservation Program Improvement Act (S 629)
votes.bill_title: Emergency Conservation Program Improvement Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill revises the Emergency Conservation Program and the Emergency Forest Restoration Program to expand eligibility for payments to agricultural producers and owners of forest land impacted by natural disasters. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Weatherizing Infrastructure in the North and Terrorism Emergency Readiness Act (H R 3106)
votes.bill_title: Weatherizing Infrastructure in the North and Terrorism Emergency Readiness Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security to develop and conduct an exercise to enhance collective domestic preparedness for and response to a terrorist attack during an extreme cold weather event (e.g., an event caused by a polar vortex when Arctic air expands southward). This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — EARLY Act Reauthorization (H R 4541)
votes.bill_title: To reauthorize the Young Women’s Breast Health Education and Awareness Requires Learning Young Act of 2009.
votes.plain_language: This bill reauthorizes and revises programs of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention that support services and education addressing breast and cervical cancer. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass — Retire through Ownership Act (S 2403)
votes.bill_title: Retire through Ownership Act
votes.plain_language: This bill lets an employee stock-ownership plan rely on an independent appraiser's value for company stock that is not publicly traded, if the appraiser follows Internal Revenue Service methods. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Refer — Impeaching Peter Brian Hegseth, Secretary of Defense, for high crimes and misdemeanors (H RES 1655)
votes.bill_title: Impeaching Peter Brian Hegseth, Secretary of Defense, for high crimes and misdemeanors.
votes.plain_language: Official question: On Motion to Refer. H.Res. 1655: Impeaching Peter Brian Hegseth, Secretary of Defense, for high crimes and misdemeanors. Result: Passed.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — National Wildlife Refuge System Invasive Species Strike Team Act (H R 4219)
votes.bill_title: National Wildlife Refuge System Invasive Species Strike Team Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill writes into law the wildlife-refuge teams that fight invasive species and requires a report to Congress. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Sunshine Protection Act (H R 139)
votes.bill_title: Sunshine Protection Act of 2025
votes.plain_language: This bill makes daylight saving time the new, permanent standard time. A Yea supports passing it in the House; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Passage — Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act (H R 8884)
votes.bill_title: Removing Barriers to Work for Disabled Americans Act
votes.plain_language: This bill restarts Social Security disability demonstration projects through 2031 and says a participant's total income cannot be reduced. A Yea passes it. A Nay votes no.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Tax Relief for Fraud Victims Act (H R 9500)
votes.bill_title: Tax Relief for Fraud Victims Act
votes.plain_language: This bill widens the tax deduction for theft and fraud losses, including losses that are not from a declared disaster, and it eases related refund and retirement-plan rules. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Improving Travel for American Families Act (H R 8897)
votes.bill_title: Improving Travel for American Families Act
votes.plain_language: This bill directs the Transportation Security Administration to establish a pilot program to implement alternative security screenings for passengers traveling with children who are 12 years old and younger. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Water Resources Development Act (H R 9497)
votes.bill_title: Water Resources Development Act of 2026
votes.plain_language: This bill authorizes Army Corps of Engineers water projects, including ports, flood control, and ecosystem work, and it creates an office to speed delivery. A two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

party_line.scope: House roll calls 1–323 of 2026 (323 votes, January 6, 2026 to November 12, 2026), from the House Clerk.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.
said_voted.note: No official X account is listed for this member in the public congress-legislators social-media file, so no posts are shown.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.

town_halls.note: There is no national town-hall dataset. Dates are not estimated.

disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
vote_scope: This is not a full career record. The cache is the latest 40 House rolls (2026, rolls 275-314) and 40 Senate votes (119th Congress, session 2, votes 217-256).
